To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relative performance of the algorithms depends on the characteristics of the input document collections; for each algorithm, there is a type of input document collection with which it is likely to perform best; and, an integrated algorithm that automatically chooses the best algorithm to execute is proposed.

(i) for joins involving large document collections, the inverted file-based join algorithms are better than the document-based join algorithms in most cases; (ii) the relative performance of the inverted file-based joins depends on the characteristics of the input document collections; (iii) an integrated algorithm is better than each of its component algorithms.

(1) for joins on textual data that involve a small number of documents and a small number of attributes, the inverted file algorithm is likely to outperform the other algorithms; (2) for joins on very large document collections, the document algorithm is likely to have the best performance if the number of attributes involved is small; and (3) for joins on large document collections, where the number of attributes is large, the document algorithm may perform better than the inverted file algorithm.

the following issues: (1) the performance analysis of three algorithms that process text-joins, (2) the performance evaluation of the three algorithms on real-life document collections, and (3) the development of an integrated algorithm that can automatically determine the most suitable algorithm to use for a given input query.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there does not exist one single algorithm that performs the best for all types of input documents, and that the best algorithm for each type of input document can be identified and used.

the performance of the three algorithms depends on the system characteristics, the input document collections and the input query, and that an integrated algorithm can be developed to select the best algorithm for the input query.

there is a tradeoff between the efficiency of processing a join operation and the amount of information that needs to be maintained for the operation.
